goals: Verify that the Circle class correctly implements JavaScript iteration protocols (Iterable and Iterator)
Verify that the Circle iterator infinitely cycles through the elements of a source array and handles edge cases like empty or missing inputs
activities: Initialize a source array [0, 1, 2] and instantiate a Circle object with it
Iterate over the Circle object using a for...of loop
Assert that each yielded element matches the expected sequence and break the loop once the expected length is reached
Initialize a source array [0, 1, 2] and instantiate a Circle object with it
Call next() on the Circle object in a loop corresponding to an extended expected sequence
Assert that each returned value matches the expected circular sequence and that done is false
Initialize a source array [0, 1, 2] and instantiate a Circle object with it
Destructure the first element from the Circle object
Assert that the destructured first element equals 0
Initialize a source array [0, 1, 2] and instantiate a Circle object with it
Call next() on the Circle object multiple times and assert it sequentially returns the elements in a circular manner with done as false
Initialize a source array [0] and instantiate a Circle object with it
Call next() on the Circle object multiple times and assert it repeatedly returns the single element with done as false
Instantiate a Circle object with an empty array
Call next() on the Circle object and assert it returns an object with done as true
Attempt to instantiate a Circle object without arguments and assert that it throws a TypeError
